citations.review_text:
There's a very nasty bug where you attempt to go prone and what your character does next is standing back up. Under enemy fire this is deadly. Doesn't matter how many times you press the prone button; until the character stands up it won't go prone.

This hurts my user experience very badly.
I would like to kindly ask the game developers to fix this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bug, thank you.

Pretty fun. Not so fun when you have to create separate loadouts for both insurgents and security where each has variations for day and night for each class (up to 8 classes) AND also it's gamemode dependent, so separate loadouts for Co-op vs PVP, as well as some other gamemodes (like outpost and survival) having separate loadouts as well.

Co-op has 8 classes. 2 teams. Day & night. That is 32 if you make 1 loadout for each class. One loadout for each class is not enough of variantion IMO, so I ended up making on average 5 loadouts for each class. That's 160 loadouts. But that's just for Co-op. I'll need to make separate loadouts for PVP, though I heard there are lots of cheaters, so I stuck with Co-op for now. (Night time maps rarely get picked, so don't bother making as many loadouts as I did for that. 2 to 3 is fine.)

Get this though. The "not so fun" part is not the part where you make the loadouts. It's when the game randomly decides to copy one of your loadouts onto another, thus replacing it. Unless I'm completely blind, there is no way to copy a loadout, so you can't just simply and quickly copy your Co-op classes into PVP. But the game sure as hell sometimes decides that the two loadouts I already have with M1 Garand are not enough and copies one of them over my AWP loadout so I need to remake it if I want to use that bolt-action rifle instead of a semi-auto WW2 rifle.

Also, sometimes the game forgets that you have a bipod on your gun. It will appear in-game, but your character doesn't use it and you can't fold it either. You have to go to the loadout menu, unequip the bipod and re-equip it. Then you have to actually resupply in-game to get the "new" loadout. Does your gun automatically come with a bipod? Great. Remove the gun and re-add it AND ALSO all the other attachments you had on it. Very fun times indeed.

Anyway, fun to play when you're actually playing it and not doing maintenance.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features microtransactions that are strictly cosmetic and do not impact gameplay or progression.

citations.review_text:
I really like the system of Proximity chat to the enemy team, it adds more variety to hilarious moments! I also enjoy that they FINALLY made shotgun distance realistic, where it can hit targets from further away and still deal a great amount of damage instead of dealing 1 hp when further than 8 feet. And yeah, there are microtransactions, but those microtransactions are all cosmetic and dont impact the actual game or the progression in it.

This game is difficult to navigate at first, because its a realistic military shooter (as in 3 shots could kill you, and you better prioritize taking cover instead of charging forward), but you get the mechanics down pretty easily. However, multiplayer is the most difficult, and i'm not gonna jump to conclusions and say "CHEATERS!!!", because its more likely sweats whove played nothing but realistic military shooters all their life. But if you want something just slightly easier, I'd recommend playing checkpoint, where its Player vs AI. And the AI is still fairly challenging enough to where you will get your head blown off if you run out in the open for more than 2 seconds. And its just unpredictable enough to where you will still get suprised by a grenade coming through a window your in, or an RPG striking your position dead-on.

And finally, I like the component of the Commander and Observer. It gives players power to turn the tides in the war, yet it has the slightest restriction being that you need one person to command the airstrikes, and one other person to radio it in, and ensure neither of them die during their call for fire support.

I highly recommend this game for its great mix of challenging and understandable, and great mix of simulation and FPS.

No slop included. Coops fun PVP is like a game of chess. No battlepass, no FOMO rotating storefront. Guns are loud as hell, hit hard, and feel good. Cosmetics are unlocked ingame through ingame money. DLC is nothing but cosmetics and there like a dollar on a sale. Gunplay's really good and immersive. Yallah Yallah.

citations.review_text:
One of the handful of shooters that works on Linux and honestly wish I could recommend the game but as it is now I can't. 

It's fun but there is a severe lack of ability to just play with friends without having to jump into the cod brained, loser filled public lobbies, try and find a community server that fits what you want, or go through to process of hosting your own server. Steam gives you the tools so we can play with friends but you guys just refuse to actually put the effort into using it.

Every update is a handful of bug fixes, maybe one or two new additions, and 10 new cosmetic dlc's. For a game that is priced at $29.99 id expect there to be enough content to back up the price tag and insane amount of "DLC's", but the game is still fairly bare bones and feels like an early access. Yeah their are a decent number of maps but most of them feel so similar 

The customization for each class is pretty awful and insanely restrictive so if you want to actually use anything alongside your primary weapon you can really only afford 1 or 2 attachments. Which can get fairly aggravating pretty fast.

Besides the insanely greedy people behind it, this game its pretty interesting. If you're going to get it, get it while its 75%+ off otherwise its just not worth the money. It's fairly optimized, its a nice mix between COD, ARMA, and other tactical FPS games but, as it is now its not worth the price. It's yet another case I wish steam gave us a mixed option. But here the con's are enough I'd rather give it a thumbs down than thumbs up.

claims.claim: Character movements, reloads, weapon swapping, and other actions are intentionally slow to emphasize a tactical feel.

citations.review_text:
I've been playing Insurgency Sandstorm since the Exodus update, and still find myself coming back at least once every summer to play. The game still feels solid to play, and the lethality of the firefights still feel amazing years later. However, if you are an avid milsim/realistic shooter player, please note that this game came out during the era of: tactical = slow and methodical. In the case of Insurgency, this means your character always feels like he has been sedated and does literally every action in slow motion. Absolutely nothing is done quickly in this game. Reloads, weapon swapping, grenade throwing, and environmental interactions all feel like they've been slowed down to artificially amplify the "tacticool" and "hardcore" nature of the game. 

The community is still solid, and I have yet to witness any notable toxicity in my 178 hours in the game. Matches still fill up quickly in NA, though if you play fairly consistently, you'll notice that you end up playing with the same guys more often than not. 

The game has been out more than long enough for people to learn the ins and outs of every map, so matches against experienced players (which is most matches since the game came out in 2018) can quickly become cases of navigating around/finding the head-peeking m240 gunner with 4000 hours on the game sniping you across the map. This wouldn't be as much of an issue if 90% of the maps weren't open fields with a few shacks strewn about as "cover". The game really shines in its chaotic urban combat, but shows its cracks in its attempt at open combat.

I would say buy the game on sale at this point in its lifespan. Content updates are free (but slow), the community is tight knit, and the combat is hectic and fun (when it's an urban map). However, the game it does show its age in a few ways. Your character feels like he was animated by an overweight Black Rifle vetbro, and the maps are heavily cheesed as players have stress tested each possible inch of them for 8 y…

Dislikes:
1. Unstable matchmaking in PvP – often strong players end up on the same team.
2. Animations and interface occasionally malfunction.
3. Low player count.

What makes the game interesting for me:
1. Low TTK.
2. Realistic setting.
3. Tactics: good sound, shoot-through walls, smoke mechanics.
4. Variety of gameplay styles.
5. Technical aspects: the game runs smoothly on Proton 9.0-4 on Linux.
6. Continuous development: released in 2018 but still gets updates.
7. Moderate character customization.

For me, intense, close-score matches in Domination make up for all the game’s flaws.

claims.claim: Co-op mode features artificial intelligence bots that can spot and shoot players through smoke and cover or spawn directly behind them.

citations.review_text:
One of my favorite realistic shooter titles of recent memory. Especially impressed by the functionality and attention to detail in the weaponry. If only the same engine and mechanics could also be used to make similar titles in other settings- Desert Storm I, Gothic Serpent, relevant modern real-world conflicts, or even WWII for that matter.

Disclosure- I spend the vast majority of my time playing co-op modes. My only gripes are that as of the current iteration (this review written on 7/2/2026, came back recently after a long absence) fire support seems like it had been changed at some point. Helicopters get shot down left and right by the bots, but they're still extremely dangerous to human players, which seems like the worst of both worlds. A-10 gun runs feel badly neutered, they no longer destroy weapon caches and seldom get kills like they used to. I don't mind when hostile fire support is in practice, just high intensity ambiance. I do mind when mine does nothing. Mixed feelings about the nerf to the mounted .50 on technicals. Liked how absolutely terrifying these weapons were, if the bots were just too dangerous while using it- then nerf the bots not the weapon.

And as for the bots themselves, they're wildly inconsistent. That's not necessarily a bad thing, keeps things interesting. The trouble is that sometimes the bots just can't decide if they're Elmer Fudd or Simo Hayha. Sometimes a bot will see and shoot you right through smoke and cover, sometimes you can camp in the same room as him and have a nice conversation with him before anyone starts shooting. Their movement can also be janky but that might just be map geometry. I repeat, not necessarily a problem, just very strange.

I LOVE HOW OTHER PLAYERS JUST APPEAR BEHIND ME AND KILL ME! NO FOOTSTEP NOISE IS PEAK!!!!!!
co-op mode is rigged af with the most op bots ever, just phantom spawning directly behind you and killing you too! 
No but really everything else about this game rules tho
